themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Obstruction Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 460% increase (z-score: 4.13)—suggesting a sudden, localized blockage problem affecting pedestrian access in Morningside Heights.
evidence: 7 obstruction complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly baseline (460% spike, z-score: 4.13)
Spike is current and acute—emerged last week and persists this week
No prior spikes in this category over 8-week period suggests new, localized condition
reporting_angles: Ground truth: walk the affected streets (likely near transit hubs or commercial corridors) to identify what is blocking sidewalks—construction debris, vendor encroachments, parked vehicles, or street furniture.
Interview 311 caller sample or local business owners to understand the specific obstruction and its impact on foot traffic.

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints surged to 10 OVER THE PAST 2 WEEKS versus a baseline of 4.0 per week (150% increase, z-score: 3.21), indicating a potential clustering of open-air drug use or dealing in the district.
evidence: 10 drug activity complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.0 weekly baseline (150% increase, z-score: 3.21)
First significant spike in drug-related 311 complaints in the 90-day dataset
Sustained concern aligns with CB budget requests for mental health and public health outreach services
reporting_angles: Map the 10 complaints geographically: are they clustered around a specific block, park (e.g., Morningside Park), or transit node?
Interview residents, local business owners, and NYPD community officers about visibility of dealers, usage patterns, and any recent triggers (e.g., displacement from other neighborhoods).

themes_detail.label: Noise Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints (across all categories) jumped to 29 OVER 3 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 13.6 per week (113% increase, z-score: 3.36), though timing is slightly older; combined with residential and street/sidewalk noise among top 311 categories, this suggests persistent noise disturbance patterns.
evidence: 29 noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 13.6 weekly baseline (113% increase, z-score: 3.36)
Noise - Residential is the #2 complaint category overall (1585 complaints over 90 days)
Noise - Street/Sidewalk is #4 category (1001 complaints), indicating systemic noise from multiple sources
reporting_angles: Identify whether spike was event-driven (concert, construction, street fair) or symptomatic of chronic noise sources (bars, restaurants, transit).
Survey residents about sleep and quality-of-life impacts; interview venue operators and NYPD about enforcement.

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Concerns
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 APPROXIMATELY 3 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.5 per week (500% increase, z-score: 5.0, severity: high), indicating potential contamination, discoloration, or taste/odor issues affecting drinking water.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints ~3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Spike is statistically severe but small in absolute volume—suggests targeted incident rather than widespread system failure
Timing coincides roughly with obstruction spike (last week/this week), raising possibility of water main work or contamination from street activity
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) to obtain water quality test results, boil water advisories, or main break reports in the district.
Interview affected residents (those who filed complaints) about symptoms: color, taste, odor, timing.
Cross-reference with DOB permit filings (392 alterations filed in last 90 days) to see if any involve plumbing or water infrastructure.

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Surge
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violation complaints jumped to 4 APPROXIMATELY 3 WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 0.5 per week (700% increase, z-score: 4.95), suggesting behavioral or operational issues in parks—possibly related to the drug activity spike or homeless encampments.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints ~3 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (700% spike, z-score: 4.95)
Timing aligns with drug activity complaints (2 weeks ago, z-score: 3.21), suggesting possible overlap in park-based issues
Community Board has standing budget request for park reconstruction and upgrades, indicating prior maintenance and safety concerns
reporting_angles: Clarify which parks (Morningside Park is the major public space; also check for Columbia University-adjacent areas): are violations related to drug use, homeless encampments, vandalism, or misuse?
Interview Parks Dept, NYPD community officers, and resident associations about conditions in parks and enforcement response.
